rationale: Close the configuration behavior's last open question with the executed restart result. The node that had committed an unpersisted configuration does not keep it across a restart over identical stores: recovery re-derives configuration state by scanning stored entries, so the record now states that relationship and keeps only the FSM-consistency question open. Unit admission is exhausted, so this is a fidelity handoff rather than a new executable unit.

b-config-change.rationale: Add the sourced recovery branch and replace the answered restart question: the configuration is not stored apart from the log, NewRaft rebuilds it by scanning configuration entries through processConfigurationLogEntry, and an executed restart over identical stores observed the node re-deriving the log-encoded single-voter configuration rather than the committed unpersisted one, so the anomaly is confined to the running instance. The residual is now the FSM state that may have applied entries under the lost configuration.
b-config-change.preserves: b-config-change keeps its owner, trigger, configuration coordinate and its edges to f-config-membership and f-commit-quorum; the three confirmed findings and the bounded restart result all rest on the same leader-side publish and entry-scan paths, and the readout behavior is unaffected.

feedback.answered: A configuration whose entry was never durably stored does not survive a restart: after a node that had committed such a configuration was restarted over the same LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and transport with a fresh FSM, it re-derived a one-voter latest configuration at index 1 whose entry is a LogConfiguration read without error, while the adopted two-voter configuration at index 3 was gone; the corresponding implication held because the restarted node did not report the adopted configuration, which excludes the explanation that the in-memory commit persists durably.
remaining: Whether an application FSM that applied entries under the in-memory configuration is consistent with the configuration re-derived after a restart is not established.
Whether the election restriction always keeps truncation above every committed configuration index is argued from source reading rather than established by execution (b-fsm-apply).

Whether the (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair can be observed as a term regression under an off-thread heartbeat, and whether the processHeartbeat shutdown branch's unanswered RPC is observable to a transport consumer (b-follower-append).

Whether an inflated pre-vote tally in a mixed-version cluster causes avoidable election churn (b-prevote), and whether a non-leader or stale peer can use TimeoutNow to cause repeated election rounds (b-leadership-transfer).

Whether any caller outside this repository depends on the configuration index reported by GetConfiguration (b-config-readout), and whether the majority-intersection reasoning covers every permitted one-at-a-time change sequence (b-commit-quorum).
feedback.rationale: The restart premise is answered at measured granularity by an executed check whose correspondence review was accepted as a bounded negative result: the property held vacuously because the restarted node reported the log-encoded configuration, which is exactly the observation the question needed. The remaining frontier is limited to liveness-shaped residuals, an FSM-consistency question, and questions that cannot be settled from this snapshot; unit admission is exhausted, so they are retained rather than converted into new obligations.
